items.content_html:
PG 1 : Reinforced Migration and Asylum Rights 

EuroMed Rights continues to ensure that regional collaboration and advocacy in relation to migration and asylum, specifically in terms of implementing the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, as well as safe and legal pathways and fundamental rights protections, will be improved. This will be achieved by supporting the work done through the Network’s members,  collaborating in regional and national programs that enable to advocate for policy analysis, evidence-based advocacy, and enhanced cooperation in critical areas such as missing migrants, migration governance and accountability. EuroMed Rights shall also help to facilitate civil society collective advocacy concerning the review of the SNIA – National Strategy for Immigration and Asylum in Morocco. Below are planned activities during the second semester of 2026. 

PG 2 : Advanced Gender Equality 

In 2026, EuroMed Rights will further push for gender equality and gender justice in the Euro-Mediterranean region through the empowerment of feminist movements, advocacy for better legislation against gender violence,  and the promotion of rights for women and LGBTQIA+. With regional collaboration, monitoring programs such as the Backlash Map, and common advocacy campaigns, EuroMed rights will seek to combat increasing hostility to gender equality in addition to building cross-border solidarity and advocating for necessary policy change. There will be an emphasis placed on preventing feminicide and working with women and youth-led organizations. 

PG 3 : Increased Accountability, Justice and Space for Civil Society 

EuroMed Rights continues, in 2026, to support civil society actors and human rights defenders facing increasing restrictions, including by strengthening documentation, advocacy, and solidarity actions, and by facilitating engagement with international mechanisms. 

PG 4 : Safeguarded Freedom, Democracy, and Space for Civil Society 

EuroMed Rights plans to strengthen democracy, freedoms and civic space across the region by supporting civil society organisations, human rights defenders, independent media and youth-led initiatives. Key priorities include supporting advocacy against restrictions on civic space in Tunisia, strengthening cooperation between independent media and press freedom in Egypt, and enhancing the capacity of CSO to engage with regional and international human rights mechanisms in Algeria. 

PG 5 : Enhanced Economic and Social Rights   

In 2026, EuroMed Rights will strengthen efforts to advance Economic and Social Rights by supporting civil society collaboration, monitoring, and policy engagement. Key initiatives include strengthening civil society engagement on economic and social rights in Tunisia, addressing economic violence against women, and supporting collaboration and youth-led advocacy on education, socio-economic inequalities, climate change and migration in Morocco. Below are a few upcoming activities. 

NB : * Some activities/ areas are not mentioned for security reasons but are detailed in the donor’s report. Please contact us for further information 

 * The activities/dates listed are subject to change, please contact us if you are interested in attending/get more information on specific activities

items.content_html:
• More than 1,200 migrants arrived in the UK in 18 small boats during the first week of March, with no uncontrolled landings recorded.  
  • 17 March 2026: 2 Ukrainian men were sentenced to 5 and 6 years of prison in the UK after running a yacht-based migrant smuggling operation across the English Channel. Authorities, including the National Crime Agency, intercepted their boat carrying 5 migrants. The smugglers charged tens of thousands of pounds per trip, falsely presenting the journey as “luxury”.   
  • Under the “one in, one out” deal, the UK returned 377 migrants to France and accepted 380, far below its target and covering only a small share of arrivals.  
  • The UK is facing arbitration in The Hague after Rwanda sued for £100 million over a scrapped migrant resettlement deal, which the UK says is no longer payable.  
  • Plans to house 300 asylum seekers at Cameron Barracks in Inverness are delayed over a dispute on licensing requirements. No arrivals have been reported. The site is part of the UK government’s strategy to reduce reliance on costly hotels, which a 2025 report found tripled asylum housing costs to £15.3 billion.

items.content_html:
• Türkiye fears that escalating tensions with Iran could spark new refugee movements, raising concerns regarding renewed migration pressure toward Europe. Recalling the large migration movements seen during the 2015 Syria crisis. 
  • 1 April, 2026: A migrant boat capsized off the coast of Bodrum, Türkiye, after reportedly attempting to evade the Coast Guard. The vessel, carrying migrants across the Aegean Sea towards Europe, ignored warnings to stop and encountered rough waters, eventually sinking. At least 18 people died, 21 were rescued, and an unknown number remain missing as search efforts continue.

items.content_html:
• Moroccans are expected to be the main beneficiaries of Spain’s plan to regularize around 500,000 undocumented migrants. They could represent about 25% of those eligible, as the largest foreign community in the country. The measure, introduced by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, targets migrants who arrived before the end of 2025 and have lived in Spain for at least five months.

• As of the 11th of March 2026, over 667,000 people have been registered as displaced. Over 78,000 Syrians have crossed into Syria, with over 7,700 Lebanese in search of safety. UNHCR has delivered 168,000 emergency items and is providing psychosocial support, but the operation is only 14% funded.

items.content_html:
• The SOS Mediterranée rescue ship, Ocean Viking, brought 100 migrants to Ancona, Italy. The group included 20 unaccompanied minors and people from Eritrea, Egypt, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. After health checks and basic assistance, 30 adults will stay in Marche, while the rest, including minors, will be relocated to other regions (including Tuscany).  
  • On the 15th of March 2026, the Italian coast guard announced that 64 migrants were rescued at sea near Lampedusa, while a 2-year-old boy from Sierra Leone remains missing. Reports indicate that roughly 2,300 migrants have arrived in Italy so far in 2026.  
  • Sea-Watch 5 disembarked all 93 rescued migrants in Trapani after a standoff with Italian authorities over port access.  
  • April 1, 2026: 19 migrants were found dead near Lampedusa, Italy, after their vessel drifted for days at sea. The coastguard rescued 58.  
  • Between the 1st of January and the 8th of April 2026, 6,524 migrants reached Italy by boat, compared with 11,419 in the same period in 2025. Despite the overall decrease, arrivals continue, including 163 migrants rescued on the 8th of April 2026, after reaching Lampedusa on six boats from Libya and Tunisia.  
  • The Italian government has placed another migrant rescue vessel, the Aurora, operated by Sea-Watch, under administrative detention. The Aurora had recently rescued 44 migrants who were stranded at sea for 6 days, with Sea-Watch criticizing European authorities for delays in rescue coordination. Additionally, they face a fine ranging between €2,000 – €10,000.   

Cet article 11/03/2026 — 17/04/2026  est apparu en premier sur EuroMed Rights.
